analysis:
Documentation-only batch.

- test.md head 2308-2535: describes test procedures for prefix records, TP, media and cluster stop ordering. It makes no security-control claims beyond the existing T-041 cache posture.
- test.md (from the range map): qualify-sdk is now five shards plus an audit of executed counts against the full suite. This is a release-gate integrity claim; the workflow and scripts/provider-test-shards.py were not supplied, so it is unverified.
- provider-release.md head 651-792: adds the cluster_runtime release block.
  - The facts step clears secret-derived GITHUB_ENV values, deletes the signing keychain and verifies its absence, checks BUNDLE_HASH, and runs the final CLI under env -i. These are positive mitigations, but the workflow and scripts are not supplied.
  - Network-fetched catalog and manifest inputs feed the block; integrity failures fail the step.
  - The block is gated per environment by *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED. Registration is canonicalized and the body is limited to 64 KiB.
  - The flagged concern is that release registration now auto-derives approvals, grants and public qualifications, conflicting with A-017/T-054's independent-qualification assumption. The threat model lacks coverage of a cluster pair boundary.
- Release-key compromise impact (A-005) appears widened.

For integration: verify scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, provider-cluster-runtime-models.py and the release-provider.yml facts step for secret isolation and gating. The platform-side derivation and catalog-eviction semantics are external.

findings.detail: provider-release.md head 653-668 says each signed release can carry `cluster_runtime` in `POST /v1/releases`. An accepting coordinator derives that build's cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications from it, and no operator posts them per build. The block comes from the release's own CLI/worker (`--list-release-models`, `--describe-runtime`) and from catalog/CDN data fetched at build time (head ~689-713). Qualifications apply to each declared family on any Apple silicon pair, not only the evidenced placement (head 662-666). This merges release publication with qualification authority. A-017/T-054 treat durable build qualification as independently approved and separate from release publication. A holder of the release key or the CI lane, or a build whose self-declared `ClusterPublicModels` or qualification records are wrong, can enable public pair serving without separate approval. No threat-model boundary, asset or threat covers cluster pair grants or public cluster routing. The coordinator-side consumers (ParseReleaseClusterRuntime, NativeRuntimeCatalogWithReleases) and the scripts are not in the supplied evidence. Fix: add a TB/threat entry for release-derived cluster approvals. State whether release-key compromise now implies public cluster qualification, keep an independent approval step or a per-environment switch bound to platform review, and record the any-pair broadening and catalog-eviction behavior (64/64/256 bounds).
findings.title: Release registration now self-derives cluster grants and public qualifications outside the modeled independent-qualification boundary
